mainTopic: Mixed-up and lost קרבנות פסח: מביאין קדשים לבית הפסול, the agent sent to find a lost פסח, and swapping registrations for mixed-up פסחים
overview: The amud opens with the גמרא on a פסח that got mixed up with בכורות. It asks how רבי שמעון can let the whole mixture be eaten under the stricter rules of a פסח, since that shrinks the בכור's eating time. The answer is that רבי שמעון holds מביאין קדשים לבית הפסול, as he rules when an אשם is mixed with שלמים. The רבנן forbid this, so רבא gives their solution: wait for a blemish, transfer the פסח's holiness onto a fat animal, and eat the rest as a בכור בעל מום. A new משנה then deals with a group that lost its פסח and sent one member to find it while they slaughtered a replacement. Who eats from which animal depends on who told whom to slaughter on their behalf and on which animal was slaughtered first. When the order is unknown, the animal in doubt is burned, but no one needs פסח שני. The משנה then explains how groups, and also two individuals, whose פסחים got mixed up can trade members and make an 'if it's ours, if it's yours' declaration. The גמרא begins with a ברייתא on the agent case that matches the משנה.

steps.title: Challenge: Eating the animals as a פסח causes needless disqualification
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון from the משנה. Eating בכורות under the stricter time limits of a פסח causes them to become disqualified unnecessarily.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: But he is bringing holy offerings to a state of disqualification!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי שמעון's ruling in the משנה, that a פסח mixed with בכורות may be eaten by כהנים under the rules of a פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור may be eaten for two days and one night, but a פסח may be eaten for only one night. If all the animals are treated like a פסח, any meat of the real בכורות left in the morning must be burned as נותר, even though by its own rules it was still fine. The question is whether you are allowed to shrink the eating time of קדשים like this.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion that analyzes the משנה
A state of disqualification. Here it means shortening an offering's eating time so it may end up burned

steps.confusionAlert: The animals are not becoming disqualified right now. The problem is that the stricter time limit creates an earlier deadline, after which kosher meat would have to be burned.

phrases.english: Gemara: But he is bringing
phrases.notes: 'He' here is the person who follows רבי שמעון's ruling.

phrases.english: holy offerings to a state of disqualification?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא קָא מַיְיתֵי קָדָשִׁים לְבֵית הַפְּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה of פסח שנתערב בבכורות.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's ruling that the mixture is eaten under the rules of a פסח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Treating the בכורות as a פסח shortens their eating time, which leads kosher meat to be burned for no reason. That should be forbidden.

steps.title: Answer: רבי שמעון follows his own view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון consistently holds that one may bring קדשים into a state of disqualification.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון follows his reasoning, for he said: one may bring holy offerings to a state of disqualification.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits that the challenge describes the result correctly. It answers that רבי שמעון simply does not see this as a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a reinterpretation of the משנה. The גמרא shows that רבי שמעון holds a general principle that allows it. The next step brings the source showing that this is his known view.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning. He is consistent with his view elsewhere

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon follows his own reasoning,
for he said: we may bring holy offerings to a state of disqualification.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Consistency with the Tanna's known position (לטעמיה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed everyone agrees it is forbidden to cause קדשים to be disqualified.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון holds it is permitted, so his ruling in the משנה is consistent.

steps.title: Source: A guilt-offering mixed with peace-offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves רבי שמעון's view from a משנה: when an אשם is mixed with שלמים, he says to slaughter all of them in the north and eat them under the stricter rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: A guilt-offering that got mixed up with peace-offerings: רבי שמעון says they should be slaughtered in the north and eaten according to the stricter of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the claim that רבי שמעון allows bringing קדשים into a state of disqualification.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם is a קדשי קדשים offering. It must be slaughtered in the north, eaten only by male כהנים in the עזרה, and eaten for only one day and night. שלמים may be eaten for two days and one night by anyone in ירושלים. Treating the שלמים like an אשם shrinks their eating time, which is exactly the same issue as in our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Guilt-offering, of the most holy level
The northern part of the עזרה, where the most holy offerings are slaughtered
According to the stricter of them

steps.whyThisMatters: This case is the classic source for the dispute over מביאין קדשים לבית הפסול, which comes up in many places in ש״ס.

phrases.english: As we learned: a guilt-offering that became mixed with peace-offerings,
Rabbi Shimon says: they should be slaughtered in the north,
phrases.notes: Slaughtering שלמים in the north is permitted, even though it is not required.

phrases.english: and they should be eaten according to the stricter of them.
phrases.notes: That is, under the rules of an אשם: one day and night, by male כהנים, in the עזרה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the claim made in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון holds מביאין קדשים לבית הפסול
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of אשם שנתערב בשלמים

steps.title: The רבנן disagree: One may not cause disqualification
steps.stepSummary: The cited משנה continues: the חכמים told רבי שמעון that one may not bring קדשים into a state of disqualification.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: one may not bring holy offerings to a state of disqualification.
steps.whatsHappening: The quoted משנה ends with the חכמים rejecting רבי שמעון's view. This sets up the next question about what the רבנן would do in our case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This confirms that the principle really is a dispute. רבי שמעון permits shrinking the eating time, and the רבנן forbid it. Because the רבנן forbid it, they cannot use רבי שמעון's solution for the פסח mixed with בכורות.

keyTerms.meaning: We may not bring (it is forbidden)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is still part of the quoted משנה from the case of אשם and שלמים. It is not a new statement of the גמרא.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אֵין מְבִיאִין קָדָשִׁים לְבֵית הַפְּסוּל.
phrases.english: They said to him: we may not bring holy offerings to a state of disqualification.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אֵין מְבִיאִין קָדָשִׁים לְבֵית הַפְּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quoted משנה by showing the opposing view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the רבנן, it is forbidden to cause קדשים to become disqualified unnecessarily.

steps.title: Question: What do the רבנן do with the mixture?
steps.stepSummary: Since the רבנן forbid shrinking the eating time, the גמרא asks what they would do with a פסח mixed with בכורות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the רבנן, how do we act?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a practical solution according to the רבנן. This sets up רבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן rejected רבי שמעון's method, but the mixture still has to be handled somehow. The difficulty is that a בכור cannot be redeemed or switched, because its holiness comes from birth. So there seems to be no simple way out.

keyTerms.meaning: How do we act? What do we do?

phrases.english: And according to the Rabbis, how do we act?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the רבנן's rejection in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical procedure for a פסח mixed with בכורות that does not cause disqualification.

steps.title: רבא's solution: Wait for a blemish and transfer the פסח's holiness
steps.stepSummary: רבא says to wait until the animals get a blemish, then bring a fat animal and transfer the פסח's holiness onto it. The original animals are then eaten under the rules of a blemished בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: We wait until they become blemished. He brings a fat animal and says: Wherever the פסח is, let its holiness fall on this one. Then he eats them under the law of a blemished בכור.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the רבנן's practical answer, which avoids shrinking any offering's eating time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once all the animals have a blemish, the פסח can be redeemed, and its holiness moves onto the new animal no matter which one the פסח was. The new animal is brought as a שלמים. A blemished בכור belongs to the כהן and is eaten as בכור בעל מום, so all the original animals can be eaten that way, and nothing is disqualified. The new animal is fat so that it is surely worth at least as much as whichever animal was the פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: A fat animal, so it is surely worth enough for the redemption
A blemished firstborn, eaten by a כהן outside the Temple

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון allows bringing קדשים into a state of disqualification, as in the case of אשם mixed with שלמים, so the whole mixture may be eaten as a פסח. The רבנן forbid it. According to רבא, they wait for a blemish, transfer the פסח's holiness to a fat animal, and eat the rest as a בכור בעל מום.
steps.confusionAlert: The בכורות themselves are not redeemed. A בכור cannot be redeemed. Only the פסח's holiness is transferred, and the בכורות are simply eaten under their own blemished status.

phrases.english: Rava said:
We wait for him until they become blemished,
and he brings a fat animal,
and he says: wherever the Pesach is,
let its holiness take effect on this one,
phrases.notes: The new animal is then brought as a שלמים.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָכֵיל לְהוּ בְּתוֹרַת בְּכוֹר בַּעַל מוּם.
phrases.english: and he eats them under the law of a blemished firstborn.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: נַמְתִּין לוֹ עַד שֶׁיּוּמְמוּ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Wait for blemishes, redeem the פסח's holiness onto a fat animal (brought as a שלמים), and eat the originals as בכור בעל מום.

steps.title: The group sends one member to find and slaughter their lost פסח
steps.stepSummary: The group tells one member to find their lost פסח and slaughter it for them. They also slaughter a replacement. Whichever animal was slaughtered first decides who eats from what.
steps.simpleTranslation: A group lost its פסח. They told one member, "Go look for it and slaughter it for us." He found it and slaughtered it. Meanwhile, they bought another animal and slaughtered it. If his was slaughtered first, he eats from his, and they eat together with him from his. If theirs was slaughtered first, they eat from theirs, and he eats from his.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic. It sets up the first version of the lost-פסח story and rules on the cases where we know which animal was slaughtered first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the group told him "slaughter for us," his animal counts for everyone if it was slaughtered first, so they all eat from it. If the group slaughtered their replacement first, that action shows they left the original animal and moved to the new one. He stays alone on his original animal.

keyTerms.meaning: A group of people signed up together on one קרבן פסח
Slaughter it on our behalf (for us)
Was slaughtered first. The order is what decides the case.

steps.confusionAlert: Each person can only eat from the one פסח he is signed up on. That is why the order of slaughter matters so much. It decides which animal each person "belongs" to.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A group whose Paschal lamb was lost
and they said to one (member)
"Go and search, and slaughter (it) for us"
and he went and found (it) and slaughtered (it)
and they took (another animal) and slaughtered (it)
if his was slaughtered first
he eats from his
phrases.notes: The other animal has no one signed up on it and gets burned.

phrases.english: and they eat with him from his
phrases.notes: He slaughtered it for all of them, as they asked.

phrases.english: And if theirs was slaughtered first
they eat from theirs
phrases.notes: By slaughtering a new animal, they pulled out of the original one.

phrases.english: and he eats from his

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ חֲבוּרָה שֶׁאָבַד פִּסְחָהּ וְאָמְרוּ לְאֶחָד צֵא וּבַקֵּשׁ וּשְׁחוֹט עָלֵינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. It is not connected to the previous discussion about פסח mixed with בכורות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the group sent him: if his animal was slaughtered first, everyone eats from it. If theirs was first, each side eats from its own animal.

steps.title: First version: nobody knows which animal was slaughtered first
steps.stepSummary: If the order is unknown, or both were slaughtered at the same moment, he eats from his. They eat from nothing, and their animal is burned. Still, they are exempt from פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: If nobody knows which was slaughtered first, or both were slaughtered at the same moment, he eats from his. They do not eat with him, and their animal must be taken out to be burned. They are exempt from bringing a פסח שני.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the first version and rules on the case where we cannot tell which animal was slaughtered first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He is safe either way. If his was first, it is his. If theirs was first, they left him on his own animal. The group is in doubt: they belong either to his animal or to theirs, and we can't tell which. So they cannot eat from either one, and their animal is burned. They still fulfilled the main obligation, because a valid פסח was offered for them either way. That is why they don't need פסח שני.

keyTerms.meaning: The place where invalid קדשים are burned
The make-up פסח, brought a month later by someone who missed the first one

steps.confusionAlert: Not eating the meat does not mean they failed to fulfill the obligation. Their part was done when a valid פסח was offered for them. Only the eating is missing, so they don't need פסח שני.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the main requirement of the קרבן פסח is fulfilled by the offering being brought for you. Eating it is not what decides whether you need פסח שני.

phrases.english: And if it is not known
which of them was slaughtered first
or both were slaughtered at the same time
he eats from his
and they do not eat with him
phrases.notes: Maybe theirs was first, which would mean they are not on his.

phrases.english: and theirs goes out to the place of burning
phrases.notes: Maybe it was second, and they really belong to his.

phrases.english: And they are exempt from performing the second Pesach.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אֵינוֹ יָדוּעַ אֵיזֶה מֵהֶן נִשְׁחַט רִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the first version, now with the order of slaughter unknown.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Order unknown in the first version: he eats from his, theirs is burned, and the group is exempt from פסח שני.

steps.title: Second version: he asks the group to slaughter for him if he is late
steps.stepSummary: Now he is the one who asks them to slaughter for him. If theirs was first, he eats with them. If his was first, each side eats from its own animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: He told them, "If I am late, go and slaughter for me." He went, found the animal, and slaughtered it. They took another animal and slaughtered it. If theirs was slaughtered first, they eat from theirs and he eats with them. If his was slaughtered first, he eats from his and they eat from theirs.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turns to a second version of the story. This time the request to slaughter on someone's behalf comes from him, not from the group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The roles are now reversed. Since he asked them to include him, their animal counts for him too if it was slaughtered first. If his animal was first, the group still eats from their own, because slaughtering a new animal shows they left the original one.

phrases.english: He said to them:
"If I am late
go and slaughter for me."
He went and found (it) and slaughtered (it)
and they took (another) and slaughtered (it).
If theirs was slaughtered first
they eat from theirs
and he eats with them
phrases.notes: He asked to be signed up on theirs.

phrases.english: And if his was slaughtered first
he eats from his
and they eat from theirs
phrases.notes: Slaughtering a different animal shows they pulled out of the original.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן אִם אֵחַרְתִּי צְאוּ וְשַׁחֲטוּ עָלַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the story with the roles reversed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When he asked them to slaughter for him: if theirs was first, everyone eats from theirs. If his was first, each side eats from its own animal.

steps.title: Second version: nobody knows which animal was slaughtered first
steps.stepSummary: If the order is unknown, the group eats from theirs. He eats nothing, and his animal is burned. He is exempt from פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: If nobody knows which was slaughtered first, or both were slaughtered at the same moment, they eat from theirs, and he does not eat with them. His animal must be taken out to be burned, and he is exempt from bringing a פסח שני.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the second version by ruling on the case where the order of slaughter is unknown.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the mirror image of the first version. The group is now the safe side, because they clearly left the original animal by slaughtering a new one. He is the one in doubt: he belongs either to their animal or to his own, and we can't tell which. So he eats nothing and his animal is burned. A valid פסח was still offered for him either way, so he is exempt from פסח שני.
steps.whatToRemember: There is a simple pattern. Whoever said "slaughter for us/me" is the one whose status depends on the order of slaughter. In the first version the group asked, so when the order is unknown, the group eats nothing and their animal is burned. In the second version he asked, so he eats nothing and his animal is burned. Either way, the side that eats nothing is exempt from פסח שני.

phrases.english: And if it is not known
which of them was slaughtered first
or both were slaughtered at the same time
they eat from theirs
and he does not eat with them.
And his goes out to the place of burning
and he is exempt from performing the second Pesach.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אֵינוֹ יָדוּעַ אֵיזֶה מֵהֶן נִשְׁחַט רִאשׁוֹן, אוֹ שֶׁשָּׁחֲטוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם כְּאֶחָד — הֵן אוֹכְלִין מִשֶּׁלָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the second version with the unknown-order case, the mirror image of step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Order unknown in the second version: the group eats from theirs, his animal is burned, and he is exempt from פסח שני.

steps.title: Both sides asked each other to slaughter
steps.stepSummary: If he told them to slaughter for him, and they told him to slaughter for them, everyone eats from the first animal slaughtered. If it is unknown which was first, both animals are burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said to them, and they said to him: they all eat from the first one. And if it is not known which of them was slaughtered first, both of them go out to the place of burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the third version of the lost-פסח case. This time each side gave the other permission to slaughter on its behalf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because each side authorized the other, everyone is registered on whichever animal was slaughtered first. A person cannot be registered on two פסחים, so the second animal has no valid owners. If we don't know which came first, we can't tell which animal is valid, so both must be burned.

keyTerms.meaning: He said to them and they said to him: both sides authorized each other
The place where invalid sacrifices are burned

steps.confusionAlert: Both animals are burned, but the people still fulfilled their פסח. One of the two animals really was valid and was slaughtered for all of them. We just don't know which one, so no one can eat it.

phrases.english: If he said to them, and they said to him,
phrases.notes: He asked them to include him in their replacement. They asked him to slaughter the original for them.

phrases.english: they all eat from the first one.
And if it is not known
which of them was slaughtered first,
both of them go out to the place of burning.
phrases.notes: Everyone is still exempt from פסח שני.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the set of cases. Steps 7-8 had only the group asking him, and steps 9-10 had only him asking them. Now both sides asked.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When both sides authorized each other, all eat from the first animal slaughtered. If the order is unknown, both animals are burned.

steps.title: Neither side asked the other
steps.stepSummary: If no one gave anyone permission, neither side is responsible for the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did not say to them and they did not say to him, they are not responsible for one another.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the last version of the case: no one authorized anyone. Each side simply eats from its own animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without permission, neither slaughter can count for the other side. He stays on the original animal. The group, by bringing a new animal, pulled out of the original one. So each side eats its own, and there is no doubt to worry about.

keyTerms.term: לֹא אָמַר לָהֶן וְלֹא אָמְרוּ לוֹ
keyTerms.meaning: Neither side said anything to the other

steps.whatToRemember: The lost-פסח case has four versions. (1) Only they asked him: whichever was slaughtered first decides. (2) Only he asked them: whichever was slaughtered first decides. (3) Both asked: all eat from the first. (4) Neither asked: each eats its own. When there is doubt about the order, the animal in question is burned, but everyone is still exempt from פסח שני.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אָמַר לָהֶן וְלֹא אָמְרוּ לוֹ —
phrases.english: If he did not say to them, and they did not say to him,
they are not responsible for one another.
phrases.notes: He eats from the original animal and they eat from the replacement.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא אָמַר לָהֶן וְלֹא אָמְרוּ לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposite of step 11: no one authorized anyone.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without any permission given, each side eats from its own animal.

steps.title: Two groups whose animals got mixed up
steps.stepSummary: Two groups mixed up their פסחים. Each group takes one animal, and each sends one of its members over to the other group.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two groups whose פסחים got mixed up: these take one for themselves, and those take one for themselves. One of these goes over to those, and one of those goes over to these.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens a new case and describes the practical setup. The words they say come in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither group knows which animal is really theirs. Trading one member gives each animal at least one of its true original owners, no matter which animal each group took. That matters because a פסח cannot be left without any of its original owners. Only an original owner can let new people register on it.

keyTerms.meaning: Groups registered together on a פסח
Draw or take hold of (an animal)

phrases.english: Two groups whose Pesach offerings got mixed up:
these draw one for themselves,
and those draw one for themselves.

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד מֵאֵלּוּ בָּא לוֹ אֵצֶל אֵלּוּ,
phrases.english: One of these comes over to those,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶחָד מֵאֵלּוּ בָּא לוֹ אֵצֶל אֵלּוּ,
phrases.english: and one of those comes over to these,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new case in the משנה: animals mixed up between groups instead of a lost animal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each group takes one animal and trades one member with the other group.

steps.title: The two-sided declaration
steps.stepSummary: Each group tells its newcomer: if this animal is ours, you leave yours and join ours. If it is yours, we leave ours and join yours.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what they say: If this פסח is ours, your hands are withdrawn from yours and you are registered on ours. And if this פסח is yours, our hands are withdrawn from ours and we are registered on yours.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the exact words each group says to the member who joined them. The declaration covers both possibilities.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the animal really belongs to the group, the newcomer withdraws from his old animal and joins theirs. If it really belongs to the newcomer's group, he is the original owner there, so the group withdraws from their own animal and joins his. Either way, everyone at the table is properly registered on the animal they are eating.

keyTerms.meaning: Your hands are withdrawn: you pull out of your registration

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'your hands are withdrawn' do not mean anyone is giving up the מצוה. They only move a person's registration from one animal to the other, so that he ends up on the right one.

phrases.english: And this is what they say:
If this Pesach offering is ours,
your hands are withdrawn from yours
and you are registered on ours.
And if this Pesach offering is yours,
our hands are withdrawn from ours
and we are registered on yours.
phrases.notes: The other group says the same thing to its newcomer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the setup of step 13 by giving the words that make the exchange work.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A conditional, two-sided declaration makes sure everyone is registered on the animal they actually eat.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key method in this area of הלכה. When we can't know the facts, a conditional statement that covers every possibility can settle the doubt ahead of time.

steps.title: The same method for five groups
steps.stepSummary: With five groups of five or ten people each, one person is drawn from every group, and they say the same declaration.
steps.simpleTranslation: And similarly, five groups of five each, or of ten each: they draw one from each and every group, and so they say.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה extends the method to more than two groups. Each group gets one member from every other group, and they make the same conditional declaration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With many groups, any animal could belong to any of them. So each table needs a representative from every group. That way an original owner is always present, whichever animal it really is. The size of each group does not matter.
steps.whatToRemember: For mixed-up פסחים: every table must include at least one member of every group. Then everyone makes the conditional 'if it's ours / if it's yours' declaration, so no one is left without a valid registration.

phrases.english: And similarly, five groups

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל חֲמִשָּׁה חֲמִשָּׁה וְשֶׁל עֲשָׂרָה עֲשָׂרָה —
phrases.english: of five each or of ten each:

phrases.aramaic: מוֹשְׁכִין לָהֶן אֶחָד מִכׇּל חֲבוּרָה וַחֲבוּרָה
phrases.english: they draw for themselves one from each and every group,
phrases.notes: Here 'one' means one person from each group.

phrases.english: and so they say.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן חָמֵשׁ חֲבוּרוֹת שֶׁל חֲמִשָּׁה חֲמִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the two-group method of steps 13-14 to many groups.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With any number of groups, each table takes one member from every group and they say the same conditional declaration.

steps.title: Two individuals whose פסחים got mixed up: each brings in an outsider
steps.stepSummary: When two single people's פסחים get mixed up, each takes one animal and adds a person from the marketplace onto it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two people whose פסחים got mixed up: each one takes one animal for himself, and each one registers a person from the marketplace onto his animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a new case. This time the mix-up is between two individuals, not two groups. Each one takes an animal and adds a stranger onto it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With groups, each group already has many members, so one member can leave and the animal still has owners. Here each animal has only one owner. So each person first adds an outsider, which guarantees that someone stays on the animal during the swap that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: draws / takes hold of (here: takes one animal for himself)
registers someone as a member on the קרבן
from the marketplace, meaning any outside person

steps.confusionAlert: Why add a stranger at all? Because each person is about to withdraw from his own animal. Without the stranger, the animal would be left with no owner at all, even for a moment. A פסח cannot be ownerless.

phrases.english: Two people whose Paschal lambs became mixed up —
this one draws one for himself
phrases.notes: Each person was the only one registered on his animal.

phrases.english: and that one draws one for himself,

phrases.aramaic: זֶה מְמַנֶּה עִמּוֹ אֶחָד מִן הַשּׁוּק
phrases.english: this one registers with him someone from the marketplace

phrases.aramaic: וְזֶה מְמַנֶּה עִמּוֹ אֶחָד מִן הַשּׁוּק,
phrases.english: and that one registers with him someone from the marketplace,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from mixed-up groups (Steps 13-15) to mixed-up individuals, which needs an extra step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each individual takes one animal and adds an outsider onto it before any swap is made.

steps.title: The swap declaration between the two individuals
steps.stepSummary: Each original owner goes to the outsider on the other animal and makes a two-sided conditional declaration.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one goes to that one, and that one goes to this one, and this is what they say: 'If this פסח is mine, you withdraw from yours and are registered on mine. If this פסח is yours, I withdraw from mine and am registered on yours.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the case of the two individuals. Each original owner makes a conditional statement with the outsider who joined the other animal. This way, whichever animal really belongs to whom, everyone ends up properly registered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody knows which animal truly belongs to which person, so the declaration covers both possibilities. Whichever possibility is true, each animal still has a valid owner: the outsider or the original owner always remains on it. This completes the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: to / next to (goes over to the other person)
your hands are withdrawn, meaning you leave your membership

steps.whatToRemember: With individuals, the trick is: first add an outsider so no animal is ever ownerless, then swap using an 'if mine, if yours' declaration that works no matter which animal is whose.

phrases.english: this one comes to that one,
phrases.notes: Each comes to the outsider registered on the other animal.

phrases.english: and that one comes to this one,
and this is what they say:
If this Paschal lamb is mine —
your hands are withdrawn from yours
and you are registered on mine,
and if this Paschal lamb is yours —
my hands are withdrawn from mine
and I am registered on yours.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the procedure begun in Step 16 by giving the actual swap declaration.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A conditional, two-sided declaration lets each person end up properly registered no matter which animal is truly his.

steps.title: The גמרא opens: a ברייתא says that when both sides gave permission, he eats from the first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: if the agent and the group each told the other to include them, he eats from the first animal slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא. The רבנן taught: If he said to them and they said to him, he eats from the first one.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is over, and the גמרא begins by quoting a ברייתא. It goes back to the earlier case of the agent and the group, where both sides told each other to include them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches the ruling of the משנה in Step 11: the first animal slaughtered counts for everyone. Notice that the ברייתא says אוֹכֵל in the singular ('he eats'), while the משנה said they all eat. The point is the same: since both sides authorized each other, the first slaughter covers them, and the second animal is burned.

keyTerms.meaning: the Talmud's discussion of the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the משנה being repeated by mistake. It is a ברייתא, an outside teaching from the time of the תנאים, that the גמרא quotes on the same case. Notice its singular wording, אוֹכֵל.

phrases.english: GEMARA. The Sages taught:
If he said to them and they said to him —
phrases.notes: The agent told the group to include him, and the group told the agent to include them.

phrases.english: he eats from the first one.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אָמַר לָהֶן וְאָמְרוּ לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the משנה ends, the גמרא returns to the agent case of Step 11 through a parallel ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When both sides gave mutual permission, the first slaughtered animal is the one eaten.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: without permission, no one is responsible for the other
steps.stepSummary: If neither side told the other to include them, neither side is responsible for the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did not say to them and they did not say to him, they are not responsible for one another.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes with the opposite case, where no permission was given by either side. This matches the משנה's ruling in Step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without permission, neither slaughter can count for the other side. So each side simply stays with, and eats, its own animal. Permission is what links the two sides together, and here there is none.
steps.whatToRemember: Mutual permission links the agent and the group, so the first slaughter covers everyone. No permission means each side is on its own animal.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אָמַר לָהֶן וְלֹא אָמְרוּ לוֹ —
phrases.english: If he did not say to them and they did not say to him —
they are not responsible for one another.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא אָמַר לָהֶן וְלֹא אָמְרוּ לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the same ברייתא, giving the opposite case to Step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without any mutual permission, each side keeps its own animal and is not affected by the other's slaughter.
